problem: Improve a tabular binary classifier when deployment features become missing more often than training features. Use a reproducible synthetic sklearn.make_classification dataset (5000 rows,20 features,5 informative,5 redundant, class balance80/20), a fixed stratified train/validation/test split, and train-only transformations. Predictors may see missingness masks but never test labels during development. Compare median imputation plus HistGradientBoostingClassifier and missingness augmentation. Optimize held-out average precision across clean and predefined missingness stress conditions under 5 CPU minutes on an Apple Silicon laptop. Propose a distinct implementable intervention, not just tuning or ensembling named algorithms. No claim of external novelty without evidence.

proposal.title: Mirrored Missingness Augmentation with Explicit Mask Columns for Deployment Shift
proposal.intervention: Augment training data only by creating four corrupted copies of each training batch using per-feature Beta(0.5,2)-sampled MCAR dropout, appending 20 binary mask indicator columns to all 40-feature inputs (original plus corrupted), and training a single HistGradientBoostingClassifier on the combined five-copy stack. Validation and test sets receive mask columns reflecting their actual missingness pattern but are never corrupted artificially.
proposal.mechanism: HistGradientBoostingClassifier handles NaN natively via surrogate splits, so corrupted features produce implicit absence-aware splits. The appended mask columns provide an explicit, non-erasable signal that survives any internal imputation fallback. Together they force the model to learn decision boundaries conditioned on whether each feature is present, rather than assuming full observability. Beta(0.5,2) sampling concentrates rates near zero but has a heavy tail, covering low-to-moderate missingness without catastrophically destroying the training signal on every copy.
proposal.assumptions: Missingness is MCAR at deployment; if it is MNAR or MAR the mask columns may encode spurious class-conditional correlations absent at test time. The informative features must not be systematically more likely to go missing than noise features in deployment, or the model learns the wrong absence pattern. Five augmented copies assumes clean signal is not overwhelmed; this breaks if the minority class is too sparse after tiling.
proposal.baseline: Median imputation followed by the same HistGradientBoostingClassifier trained on original 20 features only, evaluated under identical clean and 10/30/50 percent MCAR stress conditions on the held-out validation set.
proposal.metric: Median average precision across four validation conditions: clean, 10%, 30%, and 50% MCAR per feature. Median is used rather than mean to avoid a single catastrophic stress condition dominating selection.
proposal.falsification: Train an identical model with n_copies set to zero and mask columns fixed at zero throughout. If the augmented model does not achieve at least 2 percentage points higher average precision under 50% missingness on the validation set, the mechanism is not functioning. Additionally, permute only the mask columns at inference and measure AP drop; no drop indicates the explicit mask pathway contributes nothing and only NaN passthrough is working.
proposal.implementation:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.datasets import make_classification
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import average_precision_score

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
X, y = make_classification(n_samples=5000, n_features=20, n_informative=5, n_redundant=5, weights=[0.8,0.2], random_state=42)
X_tv, X_test, y_tv, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2, stratify=y, random_state=42)
X_train, X_val, y_train, y_val = train_test_split(X_tv, y_tv, test_size=0.25, stratify=y_tv, random_state=42)

def mirror_augment(X, rng, n_copies=4):
    parts = [np.hstack([X, np.zeros((len(X), X.shape[1]))])]
    for _ in range(n_copies):
        rates = rng.beta(0.5, 2, X.shape[1])
        mask = rng.random(X.shape) < rates
        Xc = X.astype(float).copy(); Xc[mask] = np.nan
        parts.append(np.hstack([Xc, mask.astype(float)]))
    return np.vstack(parts)

def add_mask_cols(X, rate, rng):
    Xm = X.astype(float).copy()
    mask = rng.random(Xm.shape) < rate
    Xm[mask] = np.nan
    return np.hstack([Xm, mask.astype(float)])

X_tr_aug = mirror_augment(X_train, rng)
y_tr_aug = np.tile(y_train, 5)
model = HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_iter=300, learning_rate=0.05, max_leaf_nodes=31, random_state=42)
model.fit(X_tr_aug, y_tr_aug)

val_conds = {'clean': np.hstack([X_val, np.zeros((len(X_val),20))])}
for r in [0.1, 0.3, 0.5]:
    val_conds[f'miss_{r}'] = add_mask_cols(X_val, r, rng)
scores = {k: average_precision_score(y_val, model.predict_proba(v)[:,1]) for k,v in val_conds.items()}
print(scores, 'Median:', np.median(list(scores.values())))
